exposure: lack of assistance from a health professional for early initiation breastfeeding
not receiving postcesarean counseling about early initiation of breastfeeding
cohort: 416 mothers who underwent cesarean sections in public health facilities of Gamo and Gofa zones, south Ethiopia.
finding: The prevalence of delayed breastfeeding initiation was 53.4%, and it was significantly associated with primiparity, lack of professional assistance, absence of early skin-to-skin contact, and inadequate postcesarean counseling.
mod_finding: N/A (the study focuses exclusively on mothers who gave birth by cesarean section and does not compare outcomes across different modes of birth)
followup_time: N/A (the outcome of delayed initiation of breastfeeding is assessed immediately post-delivery, but a specific timeframe for the 'last observation' after birth is not stated)
